nodes.label: Cozy Night Reading Brand Identity
nodes.rationale: The master artwork is a panda reading an open book under a draped blanket, lit only by a small flashlight, against a near-black navy field with a warm amber pool of light. The composition encodes the product promise: private, immersive, after-dark reading. A dark-dominant palette was chosen over a light one so the icon reads as a night-reading companion and sits comfortably beside a dark reader UI; the single warm light source gives the mark a focal point that survives extreme downscaling to 40px, where only the glow and the silhouette remain legible.

nodes.label: Rounded-Squircle Launch Mark
nodes.rationale: The splash imageset is not a wordmark or a full-bleed illustration: it is the app icon artwork pre-baked with its own rounded-corner squircle mask and transparent surround, so the launch screen shows the icon shape the user just tapped. Keeping the mask inside the PNG (rather than applying a corner radius in the launch storyboard or a React Native splash component) makes the same asset render identically no matter which layer draws it, at the cost of duplicating the artwork alongside AppIcon.appiconset instead of referencing it.

nodes.label: Duplicate-File-Per-Icon-Slot Workaround
nodes.rationale: Two different AppIcon slots both require a 120x120 raster: 40pt@3x and 60pt@2x (the home screen icon). The asset catalog's Contents.json requires a distinct filename for each slot entry, so the same 120px render is committed twice, as '120.png' and '120 1.png' (byte-identical, md5 102cb46e3959b3407e09e6cb1dd4fa43). The space-in-filename form is the Finder/Preview duplicate naming convention, indicating the copy was made by hand rather than by an export pipeline. Trade-off accepted: a few KB of redundancy and a fragile hand-made filename, in exchange for not needing an icon generation step. Risk: the two files can drift if the artwork is ever updated in only one place.

nodes.label: Error Fallback UI
nodes.rationale: Rendering a fallback surface from the Error Boundary keeps a component crash from taking down the whole app, and pairs the failure with an explicit user-driven retry rather than an automatic one.

nodes.label: Offline Retry Queue
nodes.rationale: Failed network requests are cached locally instead of being discarded so the user is offered a retry option and the request can be replayed once connectivity returns; this trades storage and staleness risk for no data loss on flaky mobile networks.

nodes.label: Offline-First PDF Caching
nodes.rationale: Metadata comes from the Content API but bytes come from the CDN and are stored locally on first read, so a manuscript opens instantly on repeat visits and is readable offline; the cache-check branch exists to avoid re-downloading and re-processing large files, at the cost of local storage growth and possible staleness.

nodes.label: Network Error Retry Prompt
nodes.rationale: An offline or timed-out request is separated from an auth failure: the interceptor surfaces a retry/offline prompt instead of triggering a refresh or logout, so transient connectivity never costs the user their session.

nodes.label: Transparent Token Refresh
nodes.rationale: Expiry is handled inside the HTTP interceptor, which swaps in a new access token and replays the original request, so protected screens never see a 401 and the user is not bounced to login for a routine expiry.

nodes.label: Deferred Reading Progress Sync
nodes.rationale: Reading progress is written to local storage first and pushed to the Content API only when online, so reading never blocks on the network; the server becomes eventually consistent with the device.

nodes.label: Real-Time Progress Broadcast
nodes.rationale: Reading progress travels over a persistent WebSocket for members with an open session and is mirrored to push for everyone else, so co-readers see live position without every member needing the app in the foreground.

nodes.label: Room Code Join
nodes.rationale: Rooms are entered by typing a short code rather than by invitation link or search, which keeps joining possible offline-of-context (shared verbally or in chat) while still letting the Room API gate membership server-side.

nodes.label: Preference Feedback Loop
nodes.rationale: Favoriting writes through the User Preferences API, which in turn updates the recommendation model, making explicit user signals the training input for the personalized home feed rather than relying on implicit behavior alone.

nodes.label: Unreplaced Expo Scaffold Assets
nodes.rationale: icon.png, adaptive-icon.png, splash.png and favicon.png are all still the stock Expo template graphics (grey concentric circles on a graph-paper grid, and the generic Expo cube favicon) rather than ReadPanda artwork. The project has since moved to a bare React Native setup with no app.json/app.config, so nothing in the JS tree references them; platform icons and launch screens are configured natively in the iOS project instead. They are dead scaffold files kept only because nobody pruned the original Expo template.

nodes.label: Cozy Night Reading Brand Identity
nodes.rationale: The current brand mark depicts a panda reading an illuminated open book under a blanket against a near-black backdrop, with the warm glow of the page as the only light source. The visual argument is that ReadPanda is for intimate, low-light, late-night reading rather than daytime study: it justifies the app's dark reader chrome and warm accent color, and it reads well at small icon sizes because the glowing book keeps a bright focal point on a dark field. This supersedes an earlier light/pastel kawaii direction (flat white panda face on white, green bamboo splash), which signaled a playful children's app and washed out against dark reader surfaces.

nodes.label: Deep Link Routing
nodes.rationale: Cold-start taps route through a deep link into the target content rather than the app root, so the notification's payload determines the landing screen and engagement can be attributed in analytics.

nodes.label: Foreground/Background Delivery Split
nodes.rationale: A push is rendered as an in-app notification when the app is foregrounded and as a system notification otherwise, because an OS banner over an already-open app is redundant; both branches converge on the Navigation Service so the destination is identical regardless of entry point.

nodes.label: Centralized Axios Instance with Auth Interceptor
nodes.norm_label: centralized axios instance with auth interceptor

nodes.label: Token Encryption at Rest
nodes.rationale: Both the on-device secure storage and the server-side refresh token store are annotated as encrypted at rest, so a stolen device image or a database dump alone does not yield usable credentials.

nodes.label: Forced Re-Authentication Edge Cases
nodes.rationale: Device wipe/reinstall leaves no tokens and login from another device invalidates previous refresh tokens, so the flow deliberately treats a missing or superseded token as a clean forced re-login rather than an error state.

nodes.label: Token Rotation Option
nodes.rationale: Rotation is documented as optional: issuing a fresh refresh token on every refresh shortens the window a stolen token is usable and makes replay detectable, but it costs an extra write to the token store and breaks clients that cache the old token, so the design leaves it as a toggle.

nodes.label: Cached Recent Searches
nodes.rationale: The search bar renders locally cached recent results before the network call returns, so typing feels instant and a failed or slow Search API call still shows something useful.

nodes.label: Deferred Notification Permission Prompt
nodes.rationale: Push permission is requested only at the end of onboarding, after the user has invested in signing up and picking interests, so the prompt lands with context; the flow explicitly tolerates either granted or denied without blocking entry into the main app.
